newsitem.title: GERMANY: Clinton seeks closer US-German stance on Iran.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks closer US-German stance on Iran.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said in an interview published on Thursday that the United States and Germany should seek a more common approach to countries such as Iran.

"In respect to criminal states such as Iran, we must work harder to ensure that our differences do not overshadow our much greater agreement on ways to contain terrorism and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction," he told Germany's mass circulation Bild newspaper.

The election of a moderate Shi'ite Moslem cleric, Mohammad Khatami, as Iran's new president last month is seen by some U.S. political analysts as increasing pressure on Clinton from European allies to rethink the long U.S. drive to isolate Iran as a "rogue nation".

Germany and other European countries such as France are seen using the poll results to patch up ties with Iran that were downgraded after a German court concluded in April that Iranian leaders had ordered the 1992 killing of four Iranian Kurds in a Berlin restaurant.
Before the verdict, Germany had been the main champion of the European Union's policy of "critical dialogue" with Iran, despite the U.S. policy of isolating the country.
